title: Spec a story, then plan the retest of a change
prompt: Two things for our checkout team. First, write the acceptance criteria for this story: As a customer, I want to apply a promo code at checkout so that I pay less. A code can be used once per customer. An expired code shows "This code has expired." Gift cards are out of scope. Second, we shipped this change yesterday: promo codes now apply before shipping is calculated, and the old Coupon link in the footer is removed. What should we retest after that change?
agent: claude -p in an empty project outside the repository, with spec-writer, test-planner installed
answer:
## Acceptance criteria: apply a promo code at checkout

Requirement: A customer can apply a promo code at checkout to pay less. Each code can be used once per customer, an expired code shows an error message, and gift cards are excluded.

### Main path
AC-1. Given a customer is at checkout, when they apply a promo code, then the amount they pay is lower than before the code was applied. _apply a promo code at checkout so that I pay less_

### Validation and errors
AC-2. Given a customer is at checkout, when they apply an expired code, then the message "This code has expired." is shown. _An expired code shows "This code has expired."_

### Limits
AC-3. Given a customer has already used a code once, when they apply the same code again, then the code is not applied to their order. _A code can be used once per customer_

### Open questions
- [minor] Main path: How much does a promo code reduce the amount the customer pays? Validation and errors: Does the total stay the same when an expired code is entered?
- [minor] Limits: What message does the customer see when they apply a code they have already used? Validation and errors: What happens when the customer enters a code that does not exist?

### Out of scope
- Gift cards. _Gift cards are out of scope_

---

## Regression checklist: promo codes before shipping, Coupon link removed

Change: Promo codes are now applied before shipping is calculated, and the old Coupon link has been removed from the footer.

### promo codes
1. [ ] Apply a promo code at checkout and check that shipping is calculated on the discounted amount. _promo codes now apply before shipping is calculated_

### footer
2. [ ] Check that the Coupon link no longer appears in the footer. _the old Coupon link in the footer is removed_

### Possible impact, not stated
- Do any shipping rules depend on the order value, such as a free-shipping threshold, and do they now give a different result after a discount? The change text does not name it.
- Do the order confirmation and any receipts show the same discount and shipping amounts as checkout? The change text does not name it.
- Does the page the old Coupon link opened still work if someone goes to it directly, for example from a bookmark? The change text does not name it.
- Do the once-per-customer and expired-code rules still behave the same now that the code is applied earlier? The change text does not name it.

### Open questions
- What replaces the Coupon link, if anything? Where do customers now go to find or enter a coupon?
- Are "Coupon" and "promo code" the same feature, or two separate things?

---

The story doesn't say how big the discount is or what message shows when someone reuses a code. Your Product Owner needs to answer those before the criteria are complete. I can also put both of these on a shareable page for the team.
